decision: A — one finite memory-only probe of unchanged accepted SavedLooks is worth separately preparing and reviewing. No actual defect, human loss, fix, CPU or native acceptance is established here.
why_this_changes_a_decision: Existing source permits unavailable configurations but serializes parsed remaining configurations on Add/Remove/Undo. The existing numeric-loss guards/tests cover Rename. A narrow eight-case result can establish or refuse the predicted semantic reinterpretation and determine whether a smaller guarded writer/comparator/raw Undo owner is justified. This is existing-core mutation responsibility, distinct from the closed whole-backup browser/file workflow.

findings.explanation: The metadata reader retains unsupported configurations. commit reserializes all supplied parsed data; Add carries current.looks, Remove carries remaining records, and Undo carries parsed before.looks. Only Rename scans for nonfinite numbers and negative zero. The retained MDN page describes nonfinite numbers becoming null during JSON serialization. These literals plausibly predict loss of the selected JS number meaning outside Rename; no target function or oracle was run and no user collection was inspected.
alternatives: A separately probe unchanged source, then, only if the actual fixture proves the issue, review a fail-closed target-write guard, number-aware expected comparison and raw-source removal Undo. This is smaller and can allow safe deletion of the unsafe target, but may refuse writes while unsafe unrelated records remain and does not preserve every numeric lexeme.

B pursue a full configuration-lexeme-preserving mutation serializer only if independently justified. It could allow more metadata actions without reinterpretation, but requires new scanner/duplicate-key/depth/roundtrip/staleness authority and much broader proof. No such serializer is selected now.

findings.explanation: The probe must classify observed number type, nonfinite value and negative zero and compute Object.is comparisons before serializing its evidence. Otherwise serializing Infinity or negative zero into the report can erase the distinction under investigation. Expected API refusal is an observed outcome; an unexpected harness/storage error is a first-stop refusal. This is a source-preparation duty, not a failure of a nonexistent probe.
alternatives: A use exact raw strings plus explicit value-kind/nonfinite/signed-zero tags and pre-serialization Object.is observations, preserving the eight-case evidence with a small literal oracle.
B emit only parsed numeric JSON values or operation-success labels. That is simpler but cannot faithfully establish this question, so it should be refused as an insufficient probe.
